objectives.title: Plan your integration before writing code
objectives.why: Stripe has more than one way to accept a payment or run billing — planning first avoids building the wrong shape of integration.

objectives.title: Search for the right API method instead of guessing
objectives.why: Stripe's API surface is large — searching for the method that matches your intent beats guessing an endpoint name.

objectives.title: Search Stripe's docs when the API isn't obvious
objectives.why: An answer pulled from current docs beats a remembered one that's since changed.

objectives.title: Read live data through the API
objectives.why: Pulling real account data beats assuming what's in it.

objectives.title: Write data through the API
objectives.why: Creating or updating a real Stripe object — a customer, a price, a subscription — is the integration actually doing something.

objectives.title: Issue a refund
objectives.why: Handling money going back out is as core to a payments integration as taking it in.

objectives.title: Check your balance across accounts
objectives.why: Knowing what's actually settled and available beats assuming a charge means the money is there.

objectives.title: Retrieve your account info
objectives.why: Knowing which Stripe account you're pointed at is what stops a test charge landing in production.

objectives.title: Generate a Stripe report
objectives.why: A report turns raw transactions into something you can actually reconcile or hand to finance.

bestPractices.title: Use a restricted key, not your full secret key
bestPractices.why: Stripe explicitly recommends restricted API keys for agent use — a full secret key gives write access to your entire account the moment it's connected, whereas a restricted key limits the blast radius to exactly what the integration needs.

bestPractices.title: Check a method's parameters before calling it
bestPractices.why: Looking up the exact parameters a write method expects avoids a rejected call or, worse, a call that succeeds with the wrong values.
